scope: Current local canonical data and current shelf application only; no record creation, merge, or source retrieval.
priority_method: Rank by direct usefulness to a creative reference shelf first, then by evidence/identity risk. Counts are audit signals, not defects or automatic apply instructions.

clusters.why_this_matters: The shelf's stated search entry includes visual and structural terms. Missing feature assignments and feature-element bridges reduce reliable discovery by staging image or structure.
clusters.allowed_follow_up: Select existing records for a source-bounded review proposal; keep unknowns as holds.
clusters.not_allowed: Infer imagery, structure, technique, safety practice, or a feature assignment from titles or genre alone.

clusters.why_this_matters: Credits and creator paths are valuable shelf entry points, but the current counts show that a large share of references lack linked people or a usable profile.
clusters.allowed_follow_up: Audit existing direct-credit evidence and propose isolated, source-specific review targets.
clusters.not_allowed: Resolve same-name people, add roles, or infer credits from company affiliation or secondary summaries.

clusters.why_this_matters: Chronology and original titles support edition-aware browsing and prevent search results from implying that similarly named works are the same production.
clusters.allowed_follow_up: List existing records whose own local source metadata can support a later review.
clusters.not_allowed: Guess a premiere year, translation, edition, family relation, or current availability.

clusters.why_this_matters: Catalog entries can be valuable provenance paths, but they should not be treated as read, elementized, or work-specific without direct evidence.
clusters.allowed_follow_up: Create a local status visualization and source-resolution review order only.
clusters.not_allowed: Fetch new pages in this run, promote intake records, or treat shared catalog text as individual-work evidence.

clusters.why_this_matters: The shelf needs search results to preserve distinct productions, versions, and entries rather than collapsing them because names overlap.
clusters.allowed_follow_up: Document collision-aware UI/search requirements and select evidence thresholds for a later human review.
clusters.not_allowed: Canonical merge, duplicate deletion, or identity resolution based only on matching titles.
